I wrote the 30-minute lesson on objective O3 (context and memory) at `lessons/0001-context-and-memory.html`. I couldn't count the words, so I haven't confirmed it fits the 2,700–6,750 range that counts as 30 minutes. Quiz 0002 and its key are written too.

The lesson follows one makerspace request through three places information can live:
- **Context window:** a trace shows the program re-sending the whole history on every model call, so input cost grows with each step. It also covers context rot and compaction.
- **Saved notes:** a trace where Sam's laser-training note survives from a Monday chat to a Thursday chat.
- **Retrieval:** a manual is split into chunks, and the model searches for the few it needs instead of loading all 60,000 tokens.

It also has a token-cost worked example with a faded practice task, a sort-the-item exercise, three common-mix-up boxes and three practice checks. I did not run the lesson in a browser, so the inline SVG figures and the answer buttons are untested.

The token counts in the lesson are made-up round numbers to show the shape, not measurements of your assistant. The sources are Anthropic's context-engineering post and context-management announcement, the Claude Code docs, and a RAG survey. I read the first two. The survey and the Claude Code docs appeared only in search results, and I haven't confirmed the survey supports its two in-text citations (chunk-size tuning, embeddings).
